title: Hotspot Loans Per Household in the Student Technology Device Program
content:
Hotspots in the Student Technology Device Program are loaned per household, not per student: a household holds at most the hotspot terms' limit of Mobile Hotspot Loan loans at a time, 1, whichever student the hotspot is checked out to. A hotspot is loaned on the household's statement that it has no home internet service and lasts for the school year.

## How the household limit is counted

At the moment of a hotspot checkout, the household's Mobile Hotspot Loan loans in status checked out, in repair or reported lost are counted, across all of the household's students. Loans in status returned or charged off are not counted. The limit holds whichever student the new hotspot would be checked out to.

| Hypothetical household at the moment of checkout | Mobile Hotspot Loan loans counted | Within the limit of 1 after one more hotspot |
|---|---|---|
| No hotspot loan | 0 | Yes |
| One hotspot loan in status returned | 0 | Yes |
| One hotspot loan, checked out to an older sibling | 1 | No |
| One hotspot loan in status in repair | 1 | No |
| One hotspot loan in status reported lost | 1 | No |

## The ground of the loan and its length

- **Ground**: the household's statement that it has no home internet service. The statement is the household's own.
- **Length**: the hotspot loan lasts for the school year.

## Basis questions

**Does each student in a household get a hotspot?** No. Hotspots are loaned per household; the count covers the household's Mobile Hotspot Loan loans whichever student holds them.

**Does a hotspot in repair still count?** Yes. A loan in status in repair is counted, as are loans in status checked out and reported lost.
